intel.t: Get Nevada "out of this Lombardo Trump economy": lower costs, limits on corporate home buying, a drug price cap, data centers that pay for their own power, and a governor who is not bought by billionaire donors.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: "High Flyin' Ford": corporate funded attorney general trips and the claim he missed 420 days of work, backed by an ethics complaint a panel advanced in February; Ford says every trip was disclosed and he has no regrets.
Hispanic voters, 51 to 20, and women, 48 to 37, in Emerson's September poll, plus organized labor led by the Culinary Union's door knocking.

Public safety and crime, where voters trust Lombardo by 12 points, with independents tied at 32 and no party candidate Danielle Ford at 7 percent in Noble Predictive Insights; his favorable rating of 41 to 38 trails Lombardo's 49 to 39 in Emerson.
Kamala Harris rallied for him at the Culinary Union in Las Vegas on October 22, 2026, calling him a chance to elect Nevada's first Black governor.

He trails: $1.3 million campaign cash to Lombardo's $2.8 million, nearly $2.7 million in PAC money to more than $5.8 million excluding governors groups, and $14.1 million in DGA side ads to $29.3 million for Better Nevada PAC, though his campaign outraised Lombardo's directly in the third quarter.

A record of results and restraint: education, health care, public safety and the economy, a no new taxes pledge and a record veto pen against the Democratic Legislature, paired with attacks on Ford's out of state travel.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: The "Lombardo Trump economy": high fuel, housing and health costs, his tariff remark that people should "feel a little pain," vetoes of drug cost and renter bills, and policies Ford says serve billionaire donors like Bigelow.

White voters, 51 to 38, and men, 47 to 41, in Emerson's September poll, with a 49 to 39 favorable rating; voters trust him over Ford on public safety and crime by 12 points in Noble Predictive Insights.
Hispanic voters, where he trails 20 to 51, and Trump's 37 to 55 approval among likely voters; his economic approval is 45 to 47 in Noble, and RedBox Research had him down 43 to 46 on October 23.

At an October fundraiser he said "There's no place easier to vote in the nation than Nevada. Unfortunately," reported by the Nevada Current on October 22 and pushed by the state Democratic Party; his campaign did not comment. Earlier he skipped the October 9 Carson City forum, leaving Ford at an empty podium.

He leads: $2.8 million campaign cash to Ford's $1.3 million, more than $5.8 million in PAC money to Ford's $2.7 million excluding governors groups, and $29.3 million in Better Nevada PAC ads to $14.1 million for the DGA side, though Ford outraised his campaign directly in the third quarter.

research.summary: Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo faces Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford, who would be Nevada's first Black governor, in a race the Nevada Current describes as a virtual tie by prediction market odds. Ford is running against what he calls the Lombardo Trump economy and data center tax breaks, while Lombardo, with a large money edge, is hitting Ford over a clemency request and crime.

issues.why: Ford says Nevadans cannot afford gas, groceries or rent and proposes rent deposit caps and limits on corporate home buying, while both candidates oppose raising taxes.
Ford would end data center tax breaks over energy and drought concerns, while Lombardo championed them and then curtailed some incentives by executive order in September.
Lombardo allies attack Ford for sponsoring a clemency request for a man convicted of killing a pregnant woman, which Ford says he would have voted against.
Ford supports Question 6 to enshrine abortion rights and opposes Question 7 on voter ID.
Ford would let the state negotiate some drug prices, citing a bill Lombardo vetoed.

storylines.title: Lombardo ad features Democratic DA
storylines.what: A new Lombardo ad features Clark County DA Steve Wolfson, a Democrat, saying Ford cares more about criminals than victims. Ford says Lombardo is stooping to this level.

storylines.title: Lombardo's big money edge
storylines.what: Lombardo raised about 17 million dollars in the third quarter, mostly through Better Nevada PAC, compared with 2.28 million for Ford.

storylines.title: Ford ties Lombardo to Trump
storylines.what: Ford argues Lombardo will not stand up to Trump and notes Lombardo acknowledged the Trump agenda benefits billionaires, as prediction markets show momentum for Ford.

storylines.title: Clemency case takes over the race
storylines.what: Pro Lombardo ads hit Ford for sponsoring a clemency petition for an inmate convicted in a pregnant woman's death, and Democrat Nicole Cannizzaro said she would not have sponsored it. Ford calls the attack a Willie Horton redo.

storylines.title: Ford debates an empty podium
storylines.what: Lombardo skipped a Carson City forum and Ford took questions alone for about 45 minutes, accusing the governor of being too scared to debate.

storylines.title: Lombardo curbs data center incentives
storylines.what: Lombardo issued an executive order curtailing some data center tax incentives, while Ford says he would pause them entirely.

events.title: The clemency attack
events.prompt: Ads are hammering the attorney general for sponsoring a clemency request for a man convicted of manslaughter in a pregnant woman's death. You must decide how to handle the issue.

opts.label: Call it race baiting
opts.say: Label the attack a Willie Horton redo and point to Trump's January 6 pardons.

opts.label: Explain the process
opts.say: Say the request came from the inmate's mother and the vote would have been no.

opts.label: Make it about victims
opts.say: Put victims and prosecutors on air to say the other side cares more about criminals.

events.title: Data center tax breaks
events.prompt: Data centers are drawing water and power during a drought, and voters fear higher bills. You must say what happens to their tax incentives.

opts.label: End the tax breaks
opts.say: End incentives and require data centers to build grid capacity and use clean energy.

opts.label: Trim by order
opts.say: Curtail some incentives while keeping Nevada open to the investment.

opts.label: Keep courting them
opts.say: Keep incentives in place to win jobs and diversify the economy.

events.title: Debate or skip
events.prompt: A Northern Nevada forum offers a podium for both candidates, and the frontrunner's campaign is weighing whether to show up.

opts.label: Show up and spar
opts.say: Attend and challenge the opponent on the record directly.

opts.label: Propose a TV debate
opts.say: Skip the forum but offer a single televised debate on your terms.

opts.label: Skip it
opts.say: Decline and spend the time on paid media and rural stops.

events.title: Rent and housing costs
events.prompt: Las Vegas and Reno renters are squeezed by rising rents and deposits. You must offer a housing plan.

opts.label: Cap deposits, limit buyers
opts.say: Cap rent deposits at one month and limit corporate home purchases.

opts.label: Build more units
opts.say: Speed permits and open federal land for more housing.

opts.label: Cut red tape only
opts.say: Oppose rent rules and let the market build its way out.
